chunks: As for the speech regarding the second part:

It is based on the fallacy. We do not say that he did not understand what he presented, for the man is better than that; but he intended to disguise and confuse. In his saying: 'The argument for the necessity of leadership is invalidated by the state of occultation,' because if the fact that people are with an awe-inspiring leader who manages affairs keeps them far from the ugly (wrong), and if this necessitates his presence being a necessary grace in all times and the absence of him making obligation ugly (unjust), then this would not be invalidated during the time of occultation (because in the time of occultation) obligation was not ugly despite his absence. Thus, the argument was found but the conclusion (that it is invalidated) is not, and this is a contradiction.
ai.seo_question: How does Shia theology justify the necessity of the Imam during the period of occultation?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi refutes the opponent's claim that the Imam's occultation invalidates the necessity of leadership by distinguishing between the logical validity of the proof and the physical presence of the Imam. He argues that since the obligation (Taklif) remains valid during the occultation, the Imam's role as a source of divine grace (Lutf) is not nullified, thereby preserving the theological foundation of the Imamate despite his absence from public view.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: As for the second part of his argument:

It is based on his own words. We do not say that he did not understand what he said, for he is better than that; however, he desired to misguide and disguise lunacy in lucidity, by saying, “The argument for necessity of leadership stands violated by occultation, since if the fact that an awe-inspiring Imam, who is in charge of affairs keeps people away from wrong, renders his presence a necessary grace in all ages and religious obligations without him unjust, this would be violated during occultation and conferment of obligation would not be wrong in his absence. Therefore, the argument leads to a conclusion that does not exist. And this is a contradiction.”
